chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar and Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer who said:

I said, 'What is the ruling for the consumer of usury after the evidence (is clarified to him)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be disciplined. So if he repeats, he would be disciplined. So if he repeats, he would be killed'.
ai.seo_question: What are the graduated penalties for a consumer of usury in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the graduated judicial penalties for riba, escalating from corporal discipline (adab) to execution (qatl) for persistent refusal after clear evidence. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle of ta'zir where the ruler or judge determines the severity based on the offender's persistence, distinguishing it from fixed hudud penalties. The progression underscores the seriousness of riba as a social and economic corruption requiring decisive enforcement.
